model_form_limitations.no_experiments: No physical specimens were tested; nothing here is experimental validation.
model_form_limitations.frame_vs_part: The 2-D plane-frame idealisation omits 3-D load paths, out-of-plane bending/buckling and plate action.
model_form_limitations.joints: Printed node/joint compliance and local stress concentrations are not modelled; rigid joints assumed.
model_form_limitations.anisotropy: Layer-adhesion/road-direction anisotropy is not modelled (measured printed in-plane strength used).
model_form_limitations.plasticity: Linear elasticity only; no yield plateau, strain localisation, or failure criterion beyond first yield.
model_form_limitations.time_dependence: Creep, fatigue, UV and thermal ageing are not modelled.
model_form_limitations.spatial_scatter: Material scatter is batch-uniform, not spatial; print-defect statistics absent.
model_form_limitations.buckling_model: Euler buckling with pinned-pinned effective length; no combined axial-bending interaction.
model_form_limitations.material_provenance: Feedstock distributions are literature-derived priors, not the user's measured lots.
model_form_limitations.mass_overcount: Reported mass double-counts strut overlap (F4): +20.2% at w=1 mm, +28.7% at w=2 mm, +46.6% at w=4 mm; at the shipped robust design the analytic mass is 50.7 g vs printed union ~40.5 g (+25.2%). Reported mass is therefore a conservative upper bound, not printed mass.
model_form_limitations.optimiser_scope: D validates a reduced 2-parameter family and checks the shipped 8-parameter result; it does not prove global optimality of the 8-parameter problem.

checks.title: Closed-form Phi2 vs SciPy bivariate-normal CDF (rho <= 0.95)
checks.claim: Engine's Gauss-Legendre Phi2 agrees with SciPy's independent implementation for rho <= 0.95
checks.method: 48-point GL (engine) vs scipy.stats.multivariate_normal.cdf over 24 cases

checks.title: Extreme-correlation/deep-tail Phi2 vs independent conditional 1-D quadrature
checks.claim: The engine's extreme-rho path is genuinely verified, not SciPy-vs-SciPy
checks.method: scipy.integrate.quad of phi(x)*Phi((b-rho*x)/s) over finite [a-40,a], split at the conditional median; rho=0.99/0.999 and deep tails (a down to -8); only univariate phi/Phi used in the reference
checks.tolerance: max absolute error <= 1e-8 and max relative error <= 1e-6 where reference > 1e-10
checks.observed: max abs err 2.22e-16 (worst rho,a,b=(0.99, 2.5, 2.5)); max rel err 5.61e-08
checks.notes: The engine delegates to SciPy's bivariate-normal CDF for |rho|>0.9 (and for extreme a/b); this check validates that path against independent 1-D conditional quadrature, and the independent JavaScript implementation is cross-checked in H4. The reference uses only scipy.special.ndtr and phi, never the bivariate CDF. The first validation run (2026-10-29) found ~3.1e-6 error at rho=0.99 with the original fixed 48-point GL rule, which motivated the delegation; this check is retained as a regression guard.

checks.title: Unit-cell axial stiffness vs independent pin-jointed truss estimate
checks.claim: C11 (and C22) of the X-braced cell equals the analytical truss estimate to frame-rotation accuracy
checks.method: Periodic/affine BC frame solve (6 elements, rotations free) vs C11_truss = E_s (w/L)(2 + 1/sqrt2)
checks.tolerance: relative error <= 5e-3 (frame vs pin-jointed difference grows with w)
checks.observed: max rel err 1.43e-03 over w=1..3 mm
checks.notes: Residual is the frame's rotational compatibility at shared nodes: the pin-jointed truss estimate has no bending, the frame cell must bend slightly; error is <0.15%.

checks.title: In-plane isotropy of the square X-braced cell
checks.claim: E1 == E2 for the square cell (C11 = C22)
checks.method: Two unit-strain states of the same periodic cell

checks.title: Shear stiffness vs pin-jointed truss estimate
checks.claim: G12 is of the same order and follows the same w-scaling as the truss estimate
checks.method: Simple-shear macro strain; compare with G_truss = E_s (w/L)/sqrt2
checks.observed: max rel err 3.18% over w=1..3 mm (grows with w: +0.4% at w=1, +3.2% at w=3)
checks.notes: Frame action stiffer than pin-jointed estimate for shear because shared-node rotation constraints force bending; documented, not a failure.

checks.method: Power-law fit of C11 vs w from the periodic cell

checks.title: STL strut mesh: count, finite coordinates, envelope, non-degenerate
checks.claim: 12 triangles per strut, finite vertices, inside the expected strut envelope
checks.method: lattice_triangles on uniform w=2; strut triangles = 94x12 = 1128
checks.tolerance: count == 1128; all finite; all areas > 1e-10; bounds inside [10-w/2, 150+w/2] x [-w/2, 60+w/2] x [-5,5]
checks.notes: Strut boxes extend past the nominal envelope by w/2 at diagonal ends; expected for a box-per-strut visualisation export.

checks.title: STL wall-pad mesh is the nominal 10x60x10 prism
checks.claim: Pad triangles lie inside [0,10]x[0,60]x[-5,5] and form an axis-aligned prism
checks.method: anyrb.stl._pad_triangles: pad box vertices (first 12 triangles of the export)
checks.tolerance: all pad vertex coordinates within 1e-9 of the nominal 10x60x10 box
checks.notes: REAL DEFECT (engine, stl.py): _pad_triangles builds a box whose axis runs along the pad diagonal (0,0)->(10,60) and then clips x to [0,10]; vertices land at y=0.00 and y=60.00 instead of 0..60. The pad is exported as a sheared parallelogram (signed volume still 6000 mm^3, F3), so a slicer receives a pad shifted ~5 mm out of the design envelope. The FE model and mass formula are unaffected; only the STL artifact is wrong. Recommend replacing _pad_triangles with a plain axis-aligned box (or reuse _box_triangles on the pad axis).

checks.title: STL signed volume equals the summed strut + pad volume
checks.claim: The box mesh is closed and consistently oriented; total signed volume equals the analytic sum
checks.method: Divergence-theorem volume over all 1140 triangles vs analytic sum

checks.title: Node-overlap over-count of the reported mass (known limitation, quantified)
checks.claim: mass_g sums strut volumes, double-counting strut overlap at nodes; the printed/union mass is lower
checks.method: Monte-Carlo union volume of the actual box geometry (400k samples) vs analytic sum, w=1/2/4 mm + robust design
checks.tolerance: documented, expected conservative bias; over-count < 50% and must be reported (WARN, not hidden)
checks.notes: The engine documents 'mass sums strut volumes without subtracting node overlap (conservative)'. Quantified consequence: +20.2% at w=1, +28.7% at w=2, +46.6% at w=4, +25.2% at the shipped robust design. The bias is design-dependent, so absolute mass claims and mass-based rankings can shift. Disclosure to be surfaced in the app/report: 'printed mass (union) ~40.5 g vs analytic 50.7 g (conservative)'. Recommended engine change: compute a unique union volume (clip overlapping strut segments) or report nominal-solid vs summed mass separately.
